blocks.content: Article 72 empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence.

rows: Can completely pardon, commute, remit, or suspend a death sentence.
Cannot pardon a death sentence (can only suspend, remit, or commute it).
Can grant clemency and pardon for sentences passed by Military Courts.
Has no power regarding sentences passed by a Court-Martial.
Applies to offences committed against Union Laws.
Applies to offences committed against State Laws.

items: Only the President can grant a full pardon for a death sentence; the Governor under Article 161 cannot pardon a death sentence.
The power to grant pardon or clemency for sentences awarded by a Court-Martial (military court) lies exclusively with the President.
The President acts on the advice of the Union Cabinet when deciding mercy petitions, as it is an executive power rather than a personal discretion.
A petitioner seeking mercy under Article 72 has no constitutional right to an oral hearing before the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 72 empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit, or commute sentences.
A Pardon completely absolves the convict from all sentences, punishments, and legal disqualifications.
Commutation replaces a harsher punishment with a lighter form, whereas Remission reduces the duration of a sentence without changing its character.
Respite involves awarding a lesser sentence due to special facts such as pregnancy or physical disability, while Reprieve means a temporary stay of execution.
The President exercises pardoning power on the binding advice of the Union Council of Ministers, and the decision is subject to limited judicial review.
